name: the staircase emits tiers descending and blocks ascending, and descends through a straddling coarse block
note: TypeScript-consumed in v1: conformanceSuitePaths in tools/axir/internal/axir/verify.go is a hardcoded directory list and does not include axmind, so the five generated targets do not read this file. It is run by src/ax/mind/fixtures.test.ts. Registering the suite is filed in the AxIR backlog.

log.description: A log of `preEnable` narrative steps appended BEFORE rollups were enabled, then `after` steps appended with rollups on. Every step is an `observation` from `host`.

cases.name: a fully covered log emits one coarse block, then finer ones, oldest first

expected.reason: tiers DESCEND and blocks ASCEND inside a tier, which is chronological by construction. A naive reverse of a flat segment list flips block order inside a tier and scrambles chronology under an 'oldest first' header.

cases.name: a coarse block straddling the enable marker is DESCENDED INTO, not skipped

expected.reason: tier 3 [0,27) can never seal because its oldest child is pre-enable. Skipping the segment would silently drop every summary that WAS built the moment the raw boundary crossed a fanout^k boundary; descending finds tier 2 [9,18) and [18,27) and reports the pre-enable half as a gap.

cases.name: with no rollups at all the projection degrades to a gap plus the raw tail

expected.reason: recency plus fetch-by-id is the load-bearing core; tiers are an optimisation, and losing every block degrades speed, not correctness.
